docs.name: write/bizplan
docs.text:
# Business plan

*Company name · Month Year*

## Summary

*What the business does, in two sentences.*

*Who it is for, and what they get.*

*Where it is now, and what the next year holds.*

*What you are asking for, if anything.*

## The problem

*What is hard, slow or costly for the customer today.*

*How they cope with it now.*

*Why it matters enough to pay to fix.*

## The product

*What it is and how it works, plainly.*

*What makes it better than the way things are done now.*

*What exists today, and what is still to build.*

## The market

*Who the customers are, and how many of them there are.*

*How the market is changing.*

*Who else serves them, and how you differ.*

## How it makes money

*What is sold, at what price, how often.*

*What it costs to make and to sell.*

*The margin, and how it improves with scale.*

## Going to market

*How customers hear of it.*

*How they try it, buy it and stay.*

*The first hundred customers: where they come from.*

## The team

*Who is building this, and why these people.*

*Who is missing, and when they join.*

*Advisers and partners.*

## The numbers

*Revenue and costs for the next three years, by year.*

*When it breaks even.*

*The assumptions that matter most.*

## Risks

*What could stop this working.*

*What you would do about each.*

*What you do not know yet.*

## The ask

*How much, for what, until when.*

*What it buys: the milestones.*

*What the money gets whoever gives it.*

docs.name: write/mktplan
docs.text:
# Marketing plan

*Product · Period*

## Goals

*What marketing must achieve this period, as numbers.*

*By when.*

*What success looks like, and what it does not.*

## Audience

*Who you are talking to: the two or three kinds of person.*

*What they want, worry about, and read.*

*Where they are when they decide.*

## Positioning and message

*What this is, for whom, and why it is the one to choose, in one sentence.*

*The three things to say every time.*

*The proof for each.*

## Channels

*Where the audience is, and what you will do in each place.*

*What is owned (site, list), earned (press, word of mouth) and paid (ads, sponsorship).*

*What you will not do.*

## Calendar

*What ships when: launches, campaigns, events, content.*

*The rhythm: weekly, monthly.*

*Dates that are fixed by others.*

## Budget

*How much, and where it goes, by channel.*

*People and time, not only money.*

*What you cut first if it has to shrink.*

## Measures

*The numbers you watch, and where they come from.*

*The targets for each.*

*When you look, and who decides what changes.*

docs.name: write/gtm
docs.text:
# Go-to-market plan

*Product · Launch*

## The customer

*Who buys first, exactly: role, company, situation.*

*The moment they feel the need.*

*Who else has a say in the purchase.*

## The offer

*What they get, in their words.*

*The one thing it does that nothing else does.*

*What is included, what is not, what comes later.*

## Pricing and packaging

*The price, and why that number.*

*Tiers or plans, if any, and who each is for.*

*Trials, discounts, guarantees.*

## The route to them

*How they find out: the first channel, and the second.*

*Self-serve, sales, partners, or a mix.*

*What a sale takes, step by step, and how long.*

## The launch

*What happens on the day, and the week before and after.*

*Who does what.*

*What is ready: pages, materials, support, billing.*

## Enablement

*What sales and support need to know and have.*

*The objections, and the answers.*

*The demo.*

## Measures

*Leads, trials, customers, revenue: the targets for the first month and the first quarter.*

*What a good first week looks like.*

*When you decide to push harder, change course or stop.*
